event_time.definition: The exact physical or logical instant when the financial event was executed at the source core banking rail or payment network.
event_time.timezone_policy: Strict UTC normalization. Naive timestamps are coerced to UTC; offset-bearing ISO 8601 timestamps are converted via astimezone(timezone.utc).

ingestion_time.definition: The timestamp recorded by the CF-Intelligence connector edge when the incoming payload crosses the network boundary.
ingestion_time.relationship_to_event_time: Must NEVER overwrite or conflate with event_time. Used strictly for connector SLA, latency calculation, and audit trail.

processing_time.definition: The timestamp recorded during feature store enrichment, graph insertion, model inference, or alert dispatch.

temporal_handling_policies.naive_datetime_policy: Explicit UTC assignment (dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)). Rejecting machine-local timezone assumptions to prevent silent DST / UTC offset drift.
temporal_handling_policies.future_dated_events: Tolerates clock skew up to 300 seconds. Events with event_time > current_time + 300s are tagged with future_timestamp anomaly flags.
temporal_handling_policies.out_of_order_events: Streaming graph and feature store accept out-of-order events. Edges in MultiDiGraph retain the true event timestamp. Sliding windows insert transactions and sort or filter by event time.
temporal_handling_policies.late_arriving_events: Events arriving after window expiry (t > event_time + 86400s) are recorded in persistent storage and graph topology, but do not retroactively invalidate already evaluated real-time inference scores.
temporal_handling_policies.duplicate_replay_timing: Replays or duplicate retries are deduplicated via transaction_id in the feature store, ensuring historical window velocities (velocity_1h, velocity_24h) remain mathematically invariant under network retries.
